kind: independent verification of a software property (worked example, self-issued)
subject: EverArk MVP core — resurrection soundness + fail-closed integrity
claim: On the EverArk core at the pinned commit, resurrect() returns the exact anchored state or throws FAIL-CLOSED, and never a wrong/forged state, across the tested surface below. Erasure coding is MDS (any k of n reconstruct). GF(256) is exhaustively correct. Forgery of a different state under a fixed anchor requires a SHA-256 preimage.

evidence.invariant_test: resurrect returns the true canonical state or throws — never a third value (adversarial battery)
evidence.erasure_mds: exhaustive C(n,k) subset recovery + n=255/k=254 drop-one, 0 mismatches
evidence.gf256_field: 0/65536 multiply mismatches, 0 divide, 0 EXP/LOG inverse errors vs a carryless-mul reference
evidence.manifest_binding: every manifest field bound under the 74-byte anchor (manifest_hash); all field swaps fail-closed
evidence.review: 2 red-team lanes (crypto/erasure + fail-closed) + 1 refutation pass; all findings CLOSED (F1 lossy canon, blk DoS, shape validation, sparse arrays, tiny-decode, duplicate shards, deep-nest)

out_of_scope: Verifies the OFFLINE CORE only: commitment, erasure coding, encryption, anchor binding, fail-closed resurrect. NOT the live Evernode host cluster, NPL, EVR self-funding, or the on-chain Xahau anchor write (deploy-ladder rungs 2-3, not built).
Key custody is out of scope (spec §7 open frontier): shards are useless without the secret; how the secret survives is not certified here.
Data AVAILABILITY (that >=k shards exist when needed) is an economic/operational property, not certified; only INTEGRITY (a recovered state is correct) is.
Bounded to the tested inputs + the reviewed code path; a proof for ALL inputs would require formal verification, not a test suite.
Self-issued by KVT over its own build, signed with a SAMPLE key (not the production attester). A worked example of the artifact, not a third-party engagement.

attestation.note: SAMPLE key, not the production attester
